recipes.name: Sweet and Sour Chicken Stir-Fry
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast meat - cubed
1 (8 ounce) can pineapple chunks, juice reserved

steps.text: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and stir-fry in hot oil until browned. Add carrots, bell peppers, and garlic; cook and stir for 1 to 2 minutes.

Mix soy sauce and cornstarch together in a small bowl until well combined; pour mixture into the wok or skillet. Stir in pineapple with juice, vinegar, brown sugar, and ginger. Bring to a full boil and cook until vegetables are tender and sauce is thickened.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet and Sour Chicken Stir-Fry
raw_recipe.description: This sweet-and-sour chicken stir-fry with pineapple chunks, brown sugar, soy sauce, and vinegar gets added color and flavor from carrots and peppers.

review.reviewBody: With some changes this was a very tasty dish. First of all, I followed advice gleaned from a long-ago Chinese room-mate: always stir-fry boneless chicken cubes first (and quickly over high heat), adding them back to the stir-fry once the vegetables are tender crisp. Chicken breast can be very easily overcooked. Here are the other changes I made: I minced up 2 garlic and about a one-inch piece of fresh ginger. I used half of it to stir-fry the chicken and the other half to stir fry the vegetables. Speaking of the vegetables, I added broccoli and green onion (which I had on hand)to the mix. For the sauce, I followed the advice of many reviewers and doubled the vinegar and brown sugar, also adding the juice from a larger tin of pineapple cubes. Given the extra liquid, I decided to increase the amount of cornstarch from 1 to 2 Tbsp, which was perfect. With the extra sauce, I could have added more vegetables. Next time I would increase the peppers. I served it with brown rice. A very satisfying dinner.

This recipe deserves 5 stars and I'd give more if I could. My pickiest son even loved this. I took others suggestions and doubled the sauce and got a 20 ounce can crushed pineapple and kept the soy sauce the same at 1/4 cup. I also added a heaping tablespoon of ketchup to give it that reddish color you see at restaurants. This was restaurant caliber and I'm adding it to my recipe box to make again and again in the future!

Everyone loved this! I do feel like veggies should be cooked differently - carrots first, then the peppers, then the garlic, as they don't all cook at the same rate. You could also mix together the soy sauce, cornstarch, pineapple juice, vinegar, brown sugar and ginger together instead of adding them all in individually. Other than that, the flavors were spot on. Next time I might double the sauce so we have extra to serve over the rice. Yum!

It was delicious. I did make a few changes. I used boneless, skinless chicken thighs cubed because I don't like chicken breast. I dredged the chicken thigh cubes in cornstarch before cooking. I used my wok even though it didn't specify a wok. I used gluten free tamari instead of low sodium soy sauce. I used yellow pepper instead of green pepper (but next time, I'll use green pepper for the color and they're not as sweet as yellow peppers.) All other amounts were the same as the recipe. I browned the chicken then added the carrots first for a couple of minutes, then the peppers and garlic for another 2-3 minutes. (One to 2 minutes of cooking time for the vegetables in the recipe didn't seem enough time to me and I think I was right.) I added everything else as indicated in the recipe and continued to cook and stir for another minute or two until the sauce was thickened. I served it with short grain brown rice. There was plenty of sauce, the chicken was perfectly tender and the vegetables were firm but not hard. Definitely will be repeated. I would say this amount would feed 3 people. If you want to feed 4, up the numbers a little.

Really good easy recipe. I doubled the amount of brown sugar and vinegar and used a 20 ounce can of pineapple chunks (I used half of the chunks and all of the juice). Also added another half tbsp of cornstarch & the sauce came out great. Next time I may add a pinch of red pepper flakes for a slight kick. Good recipe overall, the family enjoyed it :-)

cook the veggies after browning the chicken in the same pan? that's crazy talk. Instead, I sautéed the veggies with some olive oil separately. Then when they're just done, i.e. the peppers have a translucent look to them, I add them in with the chicken browning in a sauce pan. I doubled everything because 4 servings is never enough. I switched out the soy sauce which is too salty (even when I use low sodium) for tamari, a japanese soy sauce that is sweeter in flavor and isn't as salty. Like the other reviewers, I used chunks of pineapples instead of crush and because the can only comes in 20oz size, i forgo the vinegar. By the way, for those who hate to deal with mincing ginger (like me), I buy frozen crushed ginger cubes. They last forever and so easy to pop one out and use in any recipe. The brand name is Dorot.

Followed other suggestions, for 4 servings used 2 breasts, used 15oz of pineapple also cooked chicken in garlic, onion and ginger then removed while cooking peppers. Very good flavor and had plenty of sauce.

This was good and we will make again. Like other reviewers I doubled the sauce ingredients. I also removed the chicken from the pan while stir-frying the vegetables so that the chicken would not overcook.

I used this recipe as a starting point and made some adjustments based on what I had in the house. First off, I had time to marinate the meat beforehand. I threw the breasts (about 1.5 lbs.) into a gallon resealable plastic bag along with 1/2 cup soy sauce, 2 Tbs vinegar, 2 Tbs brown sugar and 1 tsp ground ginger. I left out the garlic because my fiance is allergic.

While this marinated in the fridge I chopped up the veggies I had on hand: carrots, celery and mushrooms. I had a 22 oz. can of pineapple slices, which I also chopped up. Increased cornstarch to 2 Tbs, used a wok and peanut oil, served over hot rice. Thanks for sharing this great recipe!

This was very good, even better than the restuarant neon-red, MSG stuff. I liked that the chicken was not fried. I used a large can of crushed pineapple b/c that is what I had. 
I also omitted the vinegar and brown sugar and used crystalized ginger. I used garlic powder and white onions. I cooked the veggies first and added the chicken (so as not to over-cook) in my wok-style pan. I added the pineapple last.
Very delicious! I owuld never think of adding ketchup, as some suggested.

Great recipe. I only used half a pound of chicken and lots of vegetables including onions and broccoli. I like to dip very small pieces of chicken in flour and then toss them in the hot oil until a little browned. I used 1 1/2 teaspoons fresh chopped ginger instead of powdered.

I made this according to the recipe and it worked easily. I'd give it an 7.5. It was good and will be remade in the future but it wasn't mind blowing. It felt like a good addition to average life's recipe book:)
We made it in the wok on the grill, fantastic. Served it over fried rice. Followed the recipe as written. Will definitely make again!!
My husband and I like Chinese food and this dish tastes pretty good. We both thought it could be a little sweeter.

I am the first to admit that I’m not a good cook. My husband cooks most of our dinner meals, but I cooked tonight and this recipe was so simple and delicious! I did make some minor modifications (we didn’t have green bell peppers, I added a little more pineapple and some peanuts for crunch), but this recipe allowed for it. Thank you for sharing this recipe!
Great taste added 1 drop of red food coloring
I'll try again
I made it exactly as printed and it was good but next time I would double the sauce and add extra ginger, sugar and vinegar.
my go-to
I loved it! But next time I'm adding more brown sugar. Needed a little more sweet.
